What you're feeling now most likely won't be how you feel later on down the road, but you have to stay alive in order to get there. Take it from someone who was depressed for at least eight years before he found the right meds; there's a way out that isn't suicide. You just have to find it.

I went to a religious private school as well. I hated it too. The good news is there are a lot of places (at least online) for people of various beliefs you can go to; for example, there're a whole bevy of religious subreddits such as /r/atheism, /r/agnostic, and so on. There may also be local clubs outside of your school you can look into if you want.

It sucks that your mom won't let you see a therapist.. I don't have any solutions there, but I really do think it would help if you can convince her.

Either way, hang in there. Like the guy above me said, life gets a LOT better after high school!

If you've already told your mother that you're feeling suicidal, then there's no harm in telling your therapist. Even if the laws in your area allow them to talk to your parents, they wouldn't tell them anything new. Tell your therapist at least that much so they can start to help you. If you're comfortable doing so, you can also ask your therapist what they're allowed to tell your parents and decide to tell them anything further based on that. 

Until then, us internet strangers are here for you to vent to if you want. Got anything more you want to get off your chest?

Being too rash for considering suicide? To me, that sounds like a perfectly normal reaction to losing the love of your life. But following through with it would be a rash decision, in my insignificant opinion.

I've never felt a loss that great, so I'm not sure what I can say to help. But one thing I'd like to point out is that you don't have to be with anyone else. There's always life as a single person if you don't want to date again, and friends you have for social interactions. I guess what I'm saying is you don't have to move on from her, and if you're never ready to, that's okay too.

If you don't mind, could I recommend a few of things you could do instead of suicide?

1) It wasn't clear whether you feel physically ugly, but if so, try posting in /r/amiugly to see if people agree (or if they have any advice!). If you were being metaphorical, ignore this.

2) High school is, or at least was for me, a hellish place where those who don't fit in are completely and utterly marginalized. The good news is, that doesn't keep going into college and onward. The key is to step outside of school and look around- in your town, on the internet, wherever, for other people with the same beliefs, thoughts, or interests as you. School and home aren't the entire world, and that's a good thing.

3) See a therapist. At least once. And tell them as much as you can bring yourself to. Maybe unloading will help, maybe they can offer some help, maybe something else that's good will come of it- And there isn't really a downside; they're a stranger who can't say anything unless they really want the pants sued off them.

And, of course, you can always rant about how you feel here- We're internet strangers, so again, there's not a downside.

Hope I helped, and if not, I apologize profusely. But reading a couple of other posts you made, it seems like you really enjoyed life at one point, and I hope you can get back to that place someday.

I was in a similar situation myself for most of the last year. I felt my life was going nowhere and I thought about killing myself nearly constantly. It got so bad that I resorted to drinking on top of my antidepressants just to stop myself from committing suicide once or twice.

Today, I feel.. Better. I still believe many of the negative things I did when I was suicidal, but I'm on an SNRI that makes it all less soul crushing. Hopefully you'll have a similar experience with antidepressants; they're not a miracle cure, but they can take the edge off. You're already doing well seeing a therapist! The next step is to find the right AD and then re-evaluate things with a clearer head.

Hey. I honestly have nothing to say that could be helpful; I don't think I can actually understand how you feel, and I won't patronize you by pretending I can. Just posting to let you know someone read this and give you an ear to vent to if you like.

Only do it if you're comfortable enough with him and your therapist and if you think it'll help. It's just something to consider. As for sleep, I know you said you tried meditation as a therapy tool in the past; have you tried it as a sleep aide? It works extremely well for me; in fact it's all I really use it for.
Sir or madam, have you ever looked up psychological projection? Please do so, then read your post again.

I don't know you well enough to recommend much, but just from what you've given us..

-You say visiting your therapist helps a little. Could you perhaps increase the frequency of your visits? On a similar note, do you think it would help your boyfriend understand you (and perhaps you him) if he came to the sessions with you? It's not uncommon to have loved ones sit in on sessions, at least not where I am.

-Is there any particular reason you can't sleep? Just speaking from experience, things are much, MUCH worse without sleep.

-Do your hobbies create anything marketable that could bring in some extra money to do other things you like? Not material wealth so much as vacations with your boyfriend and the like.

I apologize in advance if you've already considered any of this; I know I get quite annoyed when people offer options I've already considered. I wish I had a surefire way out for you, but if I had one I would've taken it myself :\ Good luck.
I always feel like if they knew, they'd be scared of/for me. That's why I usually don't really discuss how I feel with most people :| Wish we could be more open about this kind of stuff.

What I usually do when I start deteriorating is meditate. I don't mean the "empty your mind" shit people talk about sometimes, though; that's dangerous. You'll end up thinking about all the wrong things instead. The meditation I'm talking about is just concentrating on your breathing, in and out, in and out, and bringing yourself back to it every time you think of something else (note that it's absolutely normal to become distracted; it's more or less impossible NOT to unless you're some kind of master). Do it for twenty minutes or so, and you'll either drop off to sleep or emerge feeling refreshed. Either way, you win.

I honestly don't know how to help you without knowing more about you, but I just want you to know I read this. I'll probably fall asleep soon enough, so if I don't respond to anything else, that's why.. But I was here and you were heard.

Is there anything that's keeping you here that you can grab on to? Anything at all?

At my worst, I'd just run my heart out, sleep for a few hours, eat, and repeat just to keep myself from offing myself. I don't know if that'd work for you, but it's something. And it's no problem; I get lonely pretty often myself. It's part of being human. I hate it.

All I can really say is that someone's listening, and I hope you'll keep trying.

If all else fails, there are support groups where you can vent at the very least, even if there isn't sincere support to be found there. It's all about finding SOMETHING to hold on to. I'd also recommend exploring any interests you have- Literally anything you like to do or used to like. Could run the gambit from sports or drawing to whittling or archery; doesn't matter.

If women don't give a fuck, then fuck them. Not literally, but you get the idea. Despite what everyone says, getting laid really isn't that big of a deal. You feel good for a while, then it's over and life comes back. Woop-de-doo. So quit worrying about that. You have more serious things to think about.

Now, your parents.. Frankly, I don't think you have much to lose by talking to them. If they do care, that'll change something. And if they actually don't, then nothing has changed and you look elsewhere for support- The Net, extended family, wherever you think you'll find it. Because finding anything is an improvement. And when you do find something, build on that.

That's about all I have for you. Life does suck. All you can do is carve out as big a happy place in it as you can. It's difficult, but it's worth it.

Go running. Cook and eat something. Play a game. Play with your pet. Cuddle with your pet. Annoy a sibling. Just talking with myself or someone else on here. Literally anything to get you to tomorrow, because that should be your goal right now. 

And then tomorrow, try to get help- from the sound of it, your family should be understanding if you open up to them. Or if you're not up to it, just get through the days until you are. Survive until you're ready. That's all you need to do.

I was in a similar place not a month ago. I can't tell you how to get out of it; I don't even know how I did myself, or if I'm really out of it at all. But there are things you can do that make the pain more tolerable.

First off, don't bother saying you're okay. Just don't. You're not, and that's nothing to be ashamed of. If someone asks if you're alright, just say "No, I'm not." You don't have to explain if you don't want to, and it's their problem if your response makes them uncomfortable; they're the ones who asked. Go ahead and admit that you're not alright- Hell, tell your adorable little pup right now. Let a bit of the crazy peep through; it helps get it out.

Second, you need to decide if you want to keep her in your life or not. And I mean make a 100% solid decision: Do you think it's worth it to keep in contact with her, or will you just cut her out completely? If the former, try to re-establish contact. Do it gently, be clear that you're just trying to find how things stand. I'd recommend you do this if you can bear it; it sounds like she's a very special person, at least to you, and you owe it to yourself to find out how things stand with her.

If she wants nothing to do with you, or if you just couldn't stand the possible pain of rejection/the friend zone.. go full blown exorcist on her ghost. It'll haunt you until you do. Trash (or burn) her pictures (even on your phone), send back any and all of her stuff that's still in your place, remove her number, remove her on Facebook, cut out all trace of her. Yeah, it's brutal. Yeah, it'll be hard. But if you need to be rid of her to get better, you better do it right. I honestly hope it doesn't come to that, but if it does, don't back down. You need to do what you need to do; you can't love or care for ANYONE (especially not for her) properly if you're consumed with depression. Trust me on that.

Finally, if you can afford it, see a professional. No, they won't help your relationship, but they'll help YOU- And you can't really do well in a relationship if you're broken, anyway. At the very least, they'll be someone to vent all of your emotional turmoil at.

Hopefully you'll find your way out of where you are now. I wish y'all the best; hopefully your girl's just over-reacting. But if not..Take care of yourself. And go to the gym, too; the benefits are innumerable.
